Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: Any proposed Restaurant in the sub-area east of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street needs Conditional Use, with or without alcohol. Zoning district NCT-24TH-MISSION lies inside that sub-area: a conditional use (Planning Code § 249.60(f)(1), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Calle 24 Special Use District: A new Restaurant, Limited Restaurant or Bar, or the physical expansion of an existing one, is prohibited where those uses take up, or would take up with the project, more than 35% of the commercial frontage (in linear feet) within 300 feet of the site inside the district. The records do not show that share of frontage, so this is not decided (Planning Code § 249.59(d)(1), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Calle 24 Special Use District: Section 249.59 itself does not make a Restaurant, Limited Restaurant or Bar a Conditional Use; its only Conditional Use triggers are storefront mergers over 799 square feet, replacing a Legacy Business and a first-story Health Service. Whether the use needs Conditional Use comes from the underlying district table. This rule asks for nothing here (Planning Code § 249.59(d)(2), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: A Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place may serve alcohol; its licence may be transferred from inside or from outside the district. The district adds no Conditional Use for the licence itself (but see subsection (f)(1) for the Restaurant use in the sub-area). This rule asks for nothing here (Planning Code § 249.60(b)(1)(A), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: The § 202.2 operating conditions apply to every liquor establishment in the district; new, relocated or expanded ones, and any with a licence referred to Planning by ABC, must also provide outside lighting, keep window signage to 33% and keep 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades. This is a requirement, not a control (Planning Code § 249.60(d), in force since before 2022-01-01).

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State and obtain an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS online.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (corporation, $100) on the Secretary of State's bizfile portal, then apply for an EIN at irs.gov the same day (free, issued immediately Mon–Fri). The entity name and EIN are needed for every subsequent filing, the bank account, the lease, and the ABC application. File the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20 LLC, $25 corporation).

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN) and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply for a Business Registration Certificate on the Treasurer's portal using the EIN and entity name; the BAN is issued within 1–5 days and is required by every city department. File the FBN statement at the County Clerk (in person or by mail, $60–$120) if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, then publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC require the filed FBN statement.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with SF Planning to confirm (a) whether restaurant/bar frontage within 300 feet exceeds the Calle 24 SUD's 35% cap and (b) whether the concept is formula retail.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email the Current Planning front desk or use the online scheduler to request a pre-app with a planner assigned to the Mission district. Bring a lease (or letter of intent), floor plans if available, and a description of the concept including square footage, seat count, hours, and whether the business is part of a chain with 11+ locations. Ask the planner to confirm in writing whether the Calle 24 frontage cap applies and whether a formula retail CU is required. If the frontage exceeds 35%, the use is prohibited under Section 249.59(d)(1) and no CUA can be filed; confirm that finding in writing before paying any fees or signing a lease.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline of 120–300 days and government cost of $6,300–$20,900 cover the three approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval per the comparable cases, estimated $3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost and fee waiver eligibility per the catalog), Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days from application to issuance after plan check and final inspection, $470 application + $828–$2,500 plan check as of FY2026–27), and Building Permit with change of use (14–120 days for plan review and issuance, $800–$15,000 based on construction valuation). The day range is time to approval when those approvals are granted; it does not include time to a denial or withdrawal, and it assumes the Calle 24 frontage cap does not prohibit the use. The ABC Type 41 licence is not included in the path because its status is insufficient information (the transaction type is unknown and undue-concentration rules cannot be applied), but if it were a new licence or transfer from outside the census tract, add 60–180 days and $1,000–$1,600 ABC fees plus potential PCN hearing time. Also budget for entity formation and business registration ($125–$270, 1–10 days), seller's permit and EDD (free), food safety manager cert ($100–$250), RBS training for alcohol servers ($3–$30 per person), FBN filing and publication ($60–$120, 35 days), workers' comp insurance (2–6% of annual payroll), FOG interceptor installation (included in building permit construction cost), sign permit if exterior signage changes ($300–$1,500, 7–45 days), and ASCAP/BMI music licences ($600–$5,000/year combined). The cost figures are government fees only and exclude construction, architect and consultant fees, insurance premiums (except the zero-fee workers' comp registration), and rent during the approval period.

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.

records_summary: 2989 24th St sits in the NCT-24TH-MISSION zoning district where a Restaurant serving beer and wine is a conditional use; the property also falls within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which permits restaurants operating as bona fide eating places to serve alcohol, and the Calle 24 Special Use District, which may restrict new restaurants if they would push restaurant/bar frontage over 35% within 300 feet (the records do not show that share). The site currently has an active Type 21 off-sale general liquor license (a corner store or market) that has been in place since 1981. Within 500 feet there are 6 active on-sale ABC licenses and 11 registered food/drink businesses, signaling a dense commercial corridor; 27 on-sale licenses exist within 1,000 feet, raising an undue-concentration flag. Over the last 10 years only 5 dated use decisions were filed within 1,000 feet in this district—too few to compute an approval rate—but 3 of those were approved (1 outright, 2 with conditions) and 2 were withdrawn; no restaurant or bar CUA in that window was denied.
data_gaps: The Calle 24 SUD rule depends on the percentage of restaurant/bar frontage within 300 feet, but the records do not show that figure.
Conditions of approval are not extracted for most older CUA cases (pre-2018), so the specific requirements imposed on nearby restaurant approvals are unknown.
The records do not show why the two withdrawn CUA applications (2009.0649C, 2015-013516CUA) were withdrawn.
disclaimers: Permit Memo is operational guidance, not legal advice. Confirm every requirement, fee and timeline with the issuing agency before relying on it.
Items marked 'Estimated' were not verified against the agency page at the time of generation.
Timelines assume complete applications; agency backlogs, protests and corrections can extend them.
Comparable cases and statistics come from public records (DataSF, California ABC, SF Planning) as of the data date shown; records may lag agency decisions by weeks.
Statuses are set by rules from the public record and evidence labels are judgments; neither is a guarantee. Planning Commission and ABC decisions are discretionary.
